chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:
I heard him saying about the one who loses consciousness: What Allah has power over, then Allah is more entitled to excuse.

key_terms.أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ: More entitled to excuse / more deserving of pardon
key_terms.الْمَغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: The one who loses consciousness / faints
key_terms.غَلَبَ: To overpower / to have power over

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on actions or accountability for a person who loses consciousness according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'Ghalabat Allah' (divine predominance), establishing that when a person's state is entirely overpowered by Allah—such as in deep unconsciousness—they are exempt from accountability for that specific period. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational proof for the suspension of duties (taklif) during states of total incapacitation, distinguishing between voluntary negligence and involuntary divine decree. It underscores the mercy of Allah in excusing humans for what is beyond their control, reinforcing the balance between divine power and human responsibility.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/83] al-Kafi: Ali from his father AND Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Fadhl all together from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs b. al-Bukhtari from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, he (Hafs) said:
I heard him saying about the one who loses consciousness: what Allāh has power over then Allāh is more entitled to excuse.
